floor_history.headline: Recon: stale 119 migration pin killed — honest floor is 57/173 (insn-count already exact); residual is one OR-association copy + the count-1 comparand carrier, both pass-attributed from the .loop dump

Floor 57 -> 52 in pure ordinary C: declaring `complement` inside the inner loop spends loop.c's first move (threshold -= 3) so the `count - 1` comparand stays inline, which retires s1's variable-reuse

Floor 52 -> 31 in ordinary C: fold-const's associate: block aims the OR-chain constant (write it next to the OTHER term), a late `i = 0;` fixes the $s1/$s2 pair, and one arm-local `*dst++` swaps the s

Found the missing 173rd instruction: the target inlines dst++ on the COLOUR arm, not the zero-pixel arm — form f1 is 43/173 with a structurally exact inner loop, and its whole residual is a one-atom s

frontier.hypothesis: On the f1 chassis (43 / 173, structurally exact) there is an ordinary-C form that lifts pseudo 109 (dst) from 26 to >=32 reg_n_refs WITHOUT adding an instruction — and that form is the match.
frontier.mechanism: inverse.py reports the src/dst goal as a single refs_up atom on 109, and s4 proved the two families that do NOT work: tree-folded splits (`*dst = v; dst = dst + 1;`) add zero references, and distinct address forms (`dst[-1]`) add an instruction. What is left is a spelling that makes dst appear in RTL insns that the target also has — i.e. the dst reference must come from a real value the current C computes some other way. Note reg_n_refs is loop-depth weighted, so ONE extra reference inside the inner do-body is worth several units.
frontier.next_probe: On the f1 chassis, try dst spellings whose references survive to RTL without new insns: (i) make the inner-loop bound or the LoadImage argument dst-derived where it is provably equal (e.g. `LoadImage((s32)rect, (s32)dst_buf)` is the only outer-loop dst_buf use — check whether the target's 0x214-0x234 block could have come from a dst-based bound); (ii) give the blend main path `dst[0] = ...` plus a second dst-based read that the target already performs; (iii) measure each with sandbox AND re-run tools/ra_solver/extract.py + simulate.py, confirming build_insns stays 173 and 108 -> $a3 / 109 -> $a2. Do NOT re-try e1/e2/e4/e6/e3 or g1/g2 — all measured.

frontier.hypothesis: The j/complement $t4/$t5 pair and the blend-arm mflo/srl interleave are both downstream of the src/dst seat and will collapse on their own once 108/109 are right.
frontier.mechanism: The s4 side-by-side shows the blend arm's v0/v1/a0/a1 naming and the loop-bottom `lh v0,4(s0) / lh v1,6(s0) / mult v0,v1` reload differ only in which register holds what, and all of them are downstream of the a2/a3 assignment in global.c's ordering. The j/complement priorities (5789 vs 6346) are close enough that a change in the a2/a3 seats can reorder them.
frontier.next_probe: Do not spend a session on the j/complement goal or the blend interleave until the src/dst seat is settled. When it is, re-extract the model and re-run inverse.py for '{"115": 12, "116": 13}' before assuming s3's vectors still apply — the remaining untested ones are refs_down on complement by 1, live_extend on complement by 8, and refs_up on j by 2.

frontier.hypothesis: The TU that originally compiled func_8003DE14 saw a WIDER return type for DrawSync than `void`/`int`, and that changes the pressure at the call enough to move the src/dst seat.
frontier.mechanism: The f1-chassis permuter's only sub-base find (290 vs 300) was `extern void DrawSync(s32);` -> `extern long long DrawSync(s32);`. A DImode return makes the call clobber a register pair and widens the live set across the three DrawSync calls in this function. This is a prototype question, not a coercion, IF the bytes support it — the prototype-contradiction norm (memory reference sotn-prototype-struct-precedent-2026-08-10) says bytes decide the declaration.
frontier.next_probe: This is OUT OF SCOPE for a func_8003DE14-only session (the declaration lives in the shared includes and would perturb every caller in the TU). Before spending anything on it: grep the other DrawSync callers in code6cac_c2.c and check whether ANY of them show a v0/v1 pair clobber the current declaration does not predict. Only if that census is positive is it worth a measurement; a permuter score delta alone is not evidence.
